newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks higher in strong foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks higher in strong foreign buying.

text.p: The Jordanian bourse rose in active post-holiday trade on Monday sparked by resumed emerging fund activity on blue-chip mining and cement stock, dealers said.

Dealers said healthy buying orders surfaced again after a public holiday on Sunday to mark Independence Day on three industrial and mining stock which have seen gradual stepped purchases since mid-May.
The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index rose 0.33 percent to 156.73 points in high turnover of 2.4 million dinars ($3.4 million).
Three stocks alone accounted for the bulk of Monday's volume, the highest daily value since earlier this year.
Jordan Cement dominated volume with its 1,447,860 dinars worth of trade followed by lesser purchases of Jordan Phosphate Mines, and Arab Potash Co.

Brokers cite a bullish sentiment ever since the government passed a companies and securities laws earlier this month widely applauded by investors as evidence of government seriousness in accelerating moves to open the economy to foreigners.
Investment analysts say Jordan, which lagged behind others, was now gaining more attention by emerging funds as it turned from one of the most expensive to the cheapest markets in the region.
The market is now seen as undervalued compared with other regional markets such as Egypt which have seen record inflows.
"Now there are good sizeable orders by long term foreign investors," Samir Jaradat, assistant general manager for investments at Jordan Investment Finance Bank, told Reuters.
"The market continues to witness good buying by foreigners which is expected to lead to new price levels," he said.
Brokers cited the strong foreign demand encouraging some banks who own large holdings of Jordan Cement, Arab Potash and Jordan Phosphates, to sell to the funds.
Most of the activity now appears to be restricted to foreigners and some of the larger local funds with small investors falling behind, brokers said.

"Most of the buying was by large portfolios and you can feel that the small speculators were totally neutralised because of the scope of the buying surge," said Ibrahim Odeh, a broker in al-Wataniyah Financial Services.

Jordan Cement rose 0.07 dinars to 3.92 dinars for the fourth consecutive day as strong foreign interest in the blue-chip continues unabated followed by a healthy 235,026 dinars worth of trade in Jordan Phosphates, unchanged at 3.50 dinars.
The third stock which has been focus of attention, Arab Potash, rose 0.13 dinars in 182,000 dinars of trade.
Overall advancing shares outnumbered losers by 13 to 5 while 18 were unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance rose 0.01 percent to 79.70 points, 4.42 percent down from the start of the year.
